title: Parliamentary sovereignty (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: a core UK principle is that Parliament can make or unmake any law. Political and legal practice also recognises rule-of-law constraints, human rights statutes, and devolution settlements that shape how powers are exercised in practice.

title: Rule of law (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the rule of law requires accessible, predictable law, independent courts, and government action within legal authority. It is not codified in a single UK ‘constitution’ document but is enforced through statutes and case law.

title: Human Rights Act 1998 — overview (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the HRA gives effect in UK law to key ECHR rights and requires public authorities to act compatibly, with remedies in domestic courts. Declaration of incompatibility is a special parliamentary-focused remedy for primary legislation.

title: Devolution — Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: legislative competence is devolved to institutions in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland under specific statutes. Reserved and excepted matters remain primarily with Westminster; boundaries can be legally contested.
